text:
Last season Adam Gaudette, then 29 and with his fifth NHL organization, scored 17 goals in 66 games for San Jose. This season has been quieter. He has dressed for only six games, playing a bit over nine minutes a night, with no points and five shots.

Six games is far too few to judge, but the five-on-five picture is rough: the Sharks have had only 27% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about 17.5 points worse than without him. He isn't a burner by the NHL's skating data, and he rarely carries the puck in, so when his line can't win pucks below the goal line there's little else to fall back on.

What he does well is real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.4 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 83rd percentile, and Evolving-Hockey credited most of his 0.7 wins above replacement to even-strength offense. Our numbers still see a shooter worth around 10 goals the rest of the way with regular shifts. The question is whether he gets them.
headline: Adam Gaudette needs his net-front goals back
